subject: Surge-matching playbook for HorizonAI deal (tri-region capacity planning)

Cc: ops@horizonai.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: HorizonAI Q1 launch - initial capacity ask

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re aiming for a limited public launch of HorizonAssist (chat + summarization) in mid-February. We ran a quick forecast and expect an initial sustained throughput of ~260k tokens/minute with peak surges up to ~1.1M tokens/min for flash events (marketing + support). We’re planning to serve customers across US / EU / APAC.

Two asks to start:
- A tri-region Sizing recommendation (US, EU, APAC) that maps to deal tiers in the attached MRD spreadsheet.
- A short playbook for surge matching: if a flash occurs in APAC, how do we protect latency in US/EU and what fallbacks would you recommend?

Can you loop in the capacity folks and share a proposed cadence for commitments and any lead times we should expect?

Appreciate it — Aditi
Product Ops // HorizonAI

Attachments: horizon_mrd_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: HorizonAI Q1 launch - initial capacity ask

Hi Aditi — thanks for the MRD and the forecast. Looping in Laura (regional onramp) and Ben (capacity ops). We’ll put together a tri-region proposal and a concise surge playbook — plan to surface a recommended node mix, burst buffer sizing, and fallback lanes.

Quick answers up front:
- Lead times: for committed dedicated pools we typically need 8–12 weeks from signed SOW to steady-state capacity in a new region (shorter if we can reuse existing cluster capacity in a nearby region).
- Burst lanes: we can provision cross-region burst capacity for up to 4 weeks while the dedicated pool ramps. This is an add-on and priced separately.

Will target a 48-hour initial proposal and follow up with a scoped SOW draft.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Thanks — I reviewed the MRD. My initial take (high level):
- US primary: needs a baseline of 24 A100-equivalent slots (sustained) with 72-slot burst buffer to cover 3x marketing flash scenarios.
- EU primary: baseline 12 slots with 36-slot burst buffer.
- APAC (Singapore): baseline 8 slots with 48-slot burst buffer because marketing surges skew APAC morning.

Notes / tradeoffs:
- If Horizon can accept 4–6s tail latency at peaks, we can shave ~20% off committed slots by relying on cross-region KV cache warmers and short-lived routing to hosted tier.
- Quantization to int4 for smaller models will reduce footprint but requires an eval pass; don’t rely on that for initial launch.

I’ll draft the surge-matching playbook doc with fallback routing priorities and pre-warm instructions. Ben — can you validate node SKU availability and any procurement lead times for Singapore?

Laura
Director, Regional Onramp

Laura — node availability check: Singapore (APAC) has A100-derived SKUs available but procurement ETA is ~10 weeks for dedicated racks (we can shorten to 6 weeks using spot-sourced partner capacity at a higher rate). EU (Frankfurt) and US (us-west-2) are fine for 4–8 week lead times depending on exact commit.

Also flag: we should propose a tranche-based commit: Tier 1 (baseline) + Tier 2 (50% of baseline for predictable growth) + Emergency Burst (external partner capacity limited to 8 weeks). That helps Horizon manage cash flow and gives us runway on procurement.

Ben
Capacity Ops

Thanks all — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications:
1) For APAC burst, is the spot-sourced partner capacity HIPAA/ISO-friendly? We need to know compliance boundaries for our support tier customers.
2) Can you provide a cost delta between committed baseline vs baseline+tranche vs baseline+emergency burst (ballpark per region)?

We’re trying to balance the public launch promise with procurement realities. If we can keep APAC commit smaller and rely on faster partner bursts while we prove traffic, that could work — but only if the compliance profile is acceptable.

— Aditi

Subject: RE: HorizonAI Q1 launch - initial capacity ask / playbook and next steps

All — attached is a compact proposal and action list that we discussed (Soojin / Laura: please review and confirm). Key points:
- Recommended commit (initial): US baseline = 24 slots (A100-equivalent), EU baseline = 12 slots, APAC baseline = 6 slots.
- Tranche plan: Q1 commit covers baseline; month+3 commit triggers Tier2 (additional 50% capacity per region).
- Burst lanes: cross-region burst + partner-sourced emergency buffer (up to 8 weeks). Partner capacity will be restricted for regulated customers; we recommend a hybrid: keep critical-customer traffic pinned to committed nodes and route lower-tier traffic to partner burst.
- Pricing: ballpark per-region monthly committed cost (USD): US $88k, EU $42k, APAC $28k. Emergency partner bursts billed hourly; estimate peak-hour overlay ~ $150–220/hr depending on node mix.
- Next steps: Laura to deliver final playbook pages for customer SOW; Soojin to re-run commercial with these pricing bands and submit draft SOW.

Action items (short):
1) Laura: finalize surge playbook and compliant partner list — due Nov 13.
2) Ben: confirm Singapore procurement ETA and partner compliance stamps — due Nov 12.
3) Soojin: draft SOW with tranche pricing and circulate legal — due Nov 15.

Rishi
Head of Sales Engineering
